title: fhir-to-lakehouse
description: Throughput, latency, and resource usage of the fhir-to-lakehouse streaming job. See the README for the metrics it is based on.

panels.title: Resources written
panels.description: Upserted resources per second across all resource types.

panels.title: Resources deleted
panels.description: Deleted resources per second across all resource types.

panels.title: Max consumer lag
panels.description: Kafka records not yet processed by the slowest streaming query (latest offset minus processed end offset, summed over all partitions). Every query reads the whole topic, so this is the lag of the bottleneck.

targets.expr: max(sum by (query_name) (spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", type="latest", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic"}) - sum by (query_name) (spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", type="end", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic"}))

panels.title: Micro-batch duration p95
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of non-empty micro-batches across the selected queries.

panels.title: Heap after GC
panels.description: Heap still in use right after the latest GC, relative to the max heap size. This approximates the live data. Close to 100% means the driver is about to run out of memory, regardless of how full the heap looks between GCs.

panels.title: Failed Spark tasks
panels.description: Spark tasks that failed in the selected time range, e.g. because of an OutOfMemoryError. Failed tasks are retried, but usually precede a failing batch.

panels.title: Resources processed by resource type
panels.description: Resources written to or deleted from the Delta tables per second, as requested by the Kafka messages after de-duplicating each micro-batch.

panels.title: Kafka records read by query
panels.description: Kafka records (bundles) read per second by each streaming query. Each query reads every record of the subscribed topics and keeps only its resource types.

panels.title: Delta MERGE rows by action
panels.description: Rows actually inserted, updated, or deleted in the Delta tables per second, as reported by Delta. Deletes of resources that don't exist in the table aren't counted here, unlike in the panel above.

panels.title: Consumer lag by query
panels.description: Kafka records not yet processed by each streaming query, summed over all partitions. A steadily growing lag means the query can't keep up.

targets.expr: sum by (query_name) (spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", type="latest", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic"}) - sum by (query_name) (spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", type="end", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic"})

panels.title: Remaining records by topic
panels.description: Kafka records of each topic not yet processed, summed over all partitions. Every query reads the whole topic, so a topic is done once its slowest query has caught up: Remaining is the lag of that query, Records/s the processing rate of the slowest query over the last 5 minutes, and Time remaining the remaining records divided by the rate of each query. An infinite time remaining means a query has lag but made no progress in the last 5 minutes.

targets.expr: max by (topic) (sum by (query_name, topic) (spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic", type="latest"}) - sum by (query_name, topic) (spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic", type="end"}))
min by (topic) (sum by (query_name, topic) (deriv(spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic", type="end"}[5m])))

max by (topic) ((sum by (query_name, topic) (spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic", type="latest"}) - sum by (query_name, topic) (spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic", type="end"})) / (sum by (query_name, topic) (deriv(spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic", type="end"}[5m]))))

panels.title: Consumer lag by topic
panels.description: Kafka records of each topic not yet processed by the slowest streaming query, summed over all partitions. A topic whose lag doesn't go down is starved by other topics.

targets.expr: max by (topic) (sum by (query_name, topic) (spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic", type="latest"}) - sum by (query_name, topic) (spark_streaming_query_kafka_offset{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", query_name=~"$query_name", topic=~"$topic", type="end"}))

panels.title: Micro-batch duration p95 by query
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of non-empty micro-batches. Includes reading from Kafka, encoding, and all Delta operations of the batch.

panels.title: Time spent per trigger phase
panels.description: Duration of each phase of the latest trigger, averaged over the selected queries. addBatch is the time spent processing the batch in foreachBatch, walCommit and commitOffsets are checkpoint writes, latestOffset queries Kafka.

panels.title: Delta operation duration p95
panels.description: 95th percentile duration of the Delta operations by operation and resource type. MERGE time grows with the size of the target table when every MERGE rewrites most of its files, see the Delta MERGE row.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, operation, resource_type) (rate(delta_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", resource_type=~"$resource_type"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Delta operations per minute
panels.description: Number of Delta operations per minute. Each one is a commit to the table, so many small operations result in many small files.

panels.title: Average MERGE time by phase: $resource_type
panels.description: Where the time of a MERGE goes, as reported by Delta. materialize_source reads the batch and encodes the resources, which grows with the batch size. scan finds the files with rows matching the batch and reads the id column of the whole table. rewrite writes every file with a matching row again, including all unchanged rows in it. A dominating rewrite is reduced by deletion vectors or, if updates mostly hit recently written resources, by clustering the table by write time.

targets.expr: sum by (phase) (rate(delta_merge_phase_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", resource_type=~"$resource_type"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (phase) (rate(delta_merge_phase_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", resource_type=~"$resource_type"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Unchanged rows rewritten per changed row
panels.description: Delta rewrites whole files, so every updated or deleted row also writes all unchanged rows of its file again. 0 is ideal. If the number approaches the table's row count divided by the batch's changes, every MERGE rewrites the whole table. Inserts never rewrite files and aren't part of this ratio.

targets.expr: sum by (resource_type) (rate(delta_merge_rows_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", resource_type=~"$resource_type", action="copied"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (resource_type) (rate(delta_merge_rows_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", resource_type=~"$resource_type", action=~"updated|deleted"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Share of the table rewritten per MERGE
panels.description: Bytes of existing files replaced by an average MERGE, relative to the table size. Close to 100% means every MERGE rewrites the whole table, so its duration grows with the table, not with the batch. It's an approximation and can briefly exceed 100% while a table shrinks, e.g. after deletes.

targets.expr: (sum by (resource_type) (rate(delta_merge_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", resource_type=~"$resource_type", action="removed"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (resource_type) (rate(delta_merge_phase_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", resource_type=~"$resource_type", phase="rewrite"}[$__rate_interval]))) / sum by (resource_type) (max_over_time(delta_table_size_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", resource_type=~"$resource_type"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Data written by MERGE
panels.description: Bytes of new files written by MERGE per second, including rewritten unchanged rows.

panels.title: Delta table size
panels.description: Size of the current version of each table, excluding files only kept for time travel.

panels.title: Delta table files
panels.description: Number of files of the current version of each table.

panels.title: Average file size
panels.description: Many small files slow down scans, including the scan of every MERGE. Large files make every rewrite of a file more expensive. OPTIMIZE writes files of up to 1 GB by default.

targets.expr: sum by (resource_type) (delta_table_size_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", resource_type=~"$resource_type"}) / sum by (resource_type) (delta_table_files{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", resource_type=~"$resource_type"})

panels.title: JVM heap
panels.description: Used heap includes garbage and grows towards the max heap size between GCs, so it says little about memory pressure. Heap after GC approximates the live data: if it approaches the max heap size, the driver is about to fail with an OutOfMemoryError.

panels.title: JVM process memory
panels.description: Resident memory of the JVM process compared to its committed heap and non-heap memory. The difference is off-heap memory, e.g. Netty and Kafka client buffers. The container memory limit has to leave room for it on top of spark.driver.memory.

panels.title: Time spent in GC
panels.description: Share of wall-clock time spent in GC by collector. Sustained high values mean the heap is too small for the batch size. G1 Concurrent GC runs alongside the application, the other collectors pause it.

panels.title: Spark storage memory used
panels.description: Memory used by cached data, e.g. the persisted micro-batches and Delta's materialized MERGE sources.

panels.title: Spark tasks per 1000 resources
panels.description: Completed Spark tasks per 1000 processed resources. A high value means most of the time goes into scheduling tiny tasks, e.g. because the cached batches keep spark.sql.shuffle.partitions (200 by default) partitions.

panels.title: Spark tasks
panels.description: Completed and failed Spark tasks per second, and the number of running tasks.

panels.title: Shuffle data
panels.description: Shuffle data written and read per second, e.g. for de-duplicating each micro-batch and for Delta MERGE joins.
